title: Indian B2B SaaS got pipeline from founder LinkedIn, not paid — proof beat reach
content: A pre-revenue Indian B2B SaaS founder selling compliance software to mid-market ops leaders had ₹40K/month and was tempted to run LinkedIn lead-gen ads. The ads route produced cheap leads that never converted — wrong intent, long sales cycle, and a small ticket couldn't absorb paid CAC. They scrapped paid and went founder-led instead: three LinkedIn posts a week, each built around ONE real customer problem the founder had seen (a missed filing, a penalty notice), ending with a soft 'this is what we built' rather than a CTA. They also DM-ed every commenter who engaged, not to pitch but to ask a question. Over four months the account went from ~400 to ~6,000 relevant followers, and roughly 60% of qualified demos came from inbound comments and DMs — zero ad spend. The posts that worked were never feature posts; they were specific failure stories the buyer recognised.
lesson: For high-trust, long-cycle Indian B2B with a small budget, paid lead-gen burns money on wrong-intent clicks. Founder-led proof content (specific customer failure stories, not features) on LinkedIn compounds and converts — and engaging commenters by DM is the real pipeline, not the post.
